External benchmark datasets (UCI Machine Learning Repository)
=============================================================

The data files in this directory are PUBLIC benchmark datasets from the UCI
Machine Learning Repository. They are redistributed here unchanged so that the
protocol-replay experiment (code/baseline/protocol_replay.py) can be reproduced without
network access. They are NOT part of the piezoelectric nanogenerator study; they
serve only as independent, external test beds for the same modeling protocol.

Each entry lists the discrete, low-cardinality columns that were verified in the
data itself and are therefore usable as grouping variables for leave-one-level-out
or grouped k-fold cross-validation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. airfoil_self_noise.dat
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Name      : Airfoil Self-Noise Data Set
Source    : UCI Machine Learning Repository
URL       : https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/291/airfoil+self+noise
Repo DOI  : 10.24432/C5VW2C
Provenance: NASA aerodynamic and acoustic tests of airfoil blade sections
            conducted in an anechoic wind tunnel.
Citation  : Brooks, T. F., Pope, D. S., & Marcolini, M. A. (1989).
            Airfoil Self-Noise and Prediction. NASA Reference Publication 1218.
            National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
Format    : Tab-separated, 6 columns, 1503 rows, no header.
            Columns: frequency [Hz], angle of attack [deg], chord length [m],
            free-stream velocity [m/s], suction-side displacement thickness [m],
            scaled sound pressure level [dB] (target).
Groups    : free-stream velocity (4 levels), chord length (6 levels).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. ENB2012_data.xlsx
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Name      : Energy Efficiency Data Set
Source    : UCI Machine Learning Repository
URL       : https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/242/energy+efficiency
Repo DOI  : 10.24432/C51307
Provenance: Simulated energy analysis of 768 building shapes performed in
            Ecotect.
Citation  : Tsanas, A., & Xifara, A. (2012). Accurate quantitative estimation of
            energy performance of residential buildings using statistical
            machine learning tools. Energy and Buildings, 49, 560-567.
            https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enbuild.2012.03.003
Format    : Excel (.xlsx), 8 input features (X1-X8), 2 targets (Y1 heating load,
            Y2 cooling load), 768 rows.
Groups    : X7 glazing area distribution (4 levels), X1 relative compactness
            (12 levels), X5 overall height (2 levels), X6 orientation (4 levels).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Concrete_Data.xls
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Name      : Concrete Compressive Strength Data Set
Source    : UCI Machine Learning Repository
URL       : https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/165/concrete+compressive+strength
Repo DOI  : 10.24432/C5PK67
Provenance: Laboratory compression tests on concrete cylinders of varying mixture
            proportions and curing ages, donated by Prof. I-Cheng Yeh,
            Chung-Hua University, Taiwan (2007).
Citation  : Yeh, I.-C. (1998). Modeling of strength of high performance concrete
            using artificial neural networks. Cement and Concrete Research,
            28(12), 1797-1808.
            https://doi.org/10.1016/S0008-8846(98)00165-3
Format    : Excel (.xls), single sheet with header row, 1030 rows, 9 columns,
            no missing values. Columns: cement, blast furnace slag, fly ash,
            water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, fine aggregate
            [all kg per m^3 of mixture], age [days, integer], and concrete
            compressive strength [MPa] (target).
            Rows are grouped by mixture rather than randomized, so any record
            wise k-fold split must shuffle before splitting.
Groups    : age in days (14 levels: 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 56, 90, 91, 100, 120, 180,
            270, 360, 365); mixture identity, defined as the unique combination
            of the seven ingredient columns (428 levels, 1 to 20 records each);
            binder type, derived from which supplementary cementitious materials
            are present (4 levels: plain cement 232 records, slag only 334,
            fly ash only 234, slag and fly ash 230).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. yacht_hydrodynamics.data
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Name      : Yacht Hydrodynamics Data Set
Source    : UCI Machine Learning Repository
URL       : https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/243/yacht+hydrodynamics
Repo DOI  : 10.24432/C5XG7R
Provenance: Towing-tank resistance experiments on Delft systematic yacht hull
            series models, Ship Hydromechanics Laboratory, Delft University of
            Technology. Donated by Roberto Lopez.
Citation  : Gerritsma, J., Onnink, R., & Versluis, A. (1981). Geometry,
            resistance and stability of the Delft systematic yacht hull series.
            International Shipbuilding Progress, 28(328), 276-297.
            https://doi.org/10.3233/ISP-1981-2832801
            Ortigosa, I., Lopez, R., & Garcia, J. (2007). A neural networks
            approach to residuary resistance of sailing yachts prediction. In
            Proceedings of the International Conference on Marine Engineering
            (MARINE 2007), Barcelona.
Format    : Space-separated, no header, 308 rows, 7 columns, no missing values.
            Columns: longitudinal position of the centre of buoyancy, prismatic
            coefficient, length-displacement ratio, beam-draught ratio,
            length-beam ratio, Froude number, and residuary resistance per unit
            weight of displacement (target).
Groups    : hull identity, defined as the unique combination of the five
            geometry columns (22 levels, exactly 14 records each); Froude number
            (14 levels, exactly 22 records each); prismatic coefficient
            (10 levels); length-beam ratio (10 levels); length-displacement
            ratio (8 levels); longitudinal centre of buoyancy (5 levels).
            The design is a complete 22 hulls by 14 speeds grid, so leaving one
            hull out is a clean geometry-extrapolation test and leaving one
            Froude number out is a clean speed-extrapolation test.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Folds5x2_pp.xlsx
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Name      : Combined Cycle Power Plant Data Set
Source    : UCI Machine Learning Repository
URL       : https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/294/combined+cycle+power+plant
Repo DOI  : 10.24432/C5002N
Provenance: Hourly averaged sensor readings collected over six years
            (2006-2011) from a combined cycle power plant operating at full
            load, donated by Pinar Tufekci and Heysem Kaya.
Citation  : Tufekci, P. (2014). Prediction of full load electrical power output
            of a base load operated combined cycle power plant using machine
            learning methods. International Journal of Electrical Power and
            Energy Systems, 60, 126-140.
            https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijepes.2014.02.027
            Kaya, H., Tufekci, P., & Gurgen, S. F. (2012). Local and global
            learning methods for predicting power of a combined gas and steam
            turbine. In Proceedings of the International Conference on Emerging
            Trends in Computer and Electronics Engineering (ICETCEE 2012),
            13-18, Dubai.
Format    : Excel (.xlsx) with five sheets. Each sheet holds the same 9568
            records in a different random order, provided by the donors for
            5x2-fold testing, so exactly one sheet must be used at a time.
            Columns: AT ambient temperature [C], V exhaust vacuum [cm Hg],
            AP ambient pressure [mbar], RH relative humidity [%], and PE net
            hourly electrical energy output [MW] (target). No missing values;
            41 exactly duplicated records are present in the original data and
            are retained unchanged.
Groups    : all four inputs are continuous, so no native discrete column exists.
            Grouped splits therefore use a binned operating-regime variable
            computed from the data: ambient temperature in 5 C bands
            (8 levels spanning 0 to 35 C) or exhaust vacuum in 5 cm Hg bands
            (12 levels spanning 25 to 80). Leaving out a temperature band is an
            extrapolation test and is much harder than a record-wise split.

License / terms
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UCI Machine Learning Repository datasets are distributed under the
Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.
The datasets are provided here under those original terms. Please cite the
original publications listed above when using these files. The Concrete
Compressive Strength data carry the additional condition set by the donor that
reuse is unlimited provided the copyright notice for Prof. I-Cheng Yeh and the
1998 Cement and Concrete Research paper are retained, which the citation above
satisfies.
